presentation.title: Git Repository Practice
presentation.description: Eight commands take one change from your editor to GitHub, then undo it and recover it. The console shows what happens; this side explains what it means.
presentation.subject: git

commentary.text: git status reads the repository and reports what has changed. It never modifies anything, so it is always safe to run.
HeaderFix.jsx has edits that are not staged, and NewCanary.jsx is new and untracked. Only the edit to HeaderFix.jsx belongs in this lesson's commit.

commentary.text: Local main is back at a1b2c3d. Commit 7a3c91d is no longer on main, though origin/main still points to it because it was pushed. Any uncommitted work would have been lost for good.

risk.guidance: Run git status first, and stash or commit any work you want to keep.

commentary.text: The commit is back and main matches origin/main again. Using the command to rescue work does not make it safe: it still overwrites the index and working tree, so uncommitted changes would be lost.

risk.guidance: Confirm the target commit in your own reflog and preserve uncommitted work before continuing.
